article_title: Towards Data-Informed Teaching Practice: A Model for Integrating Analytics with Teacher Inquiry
citation: Saar, M., Rodríguez-Triana, M. J., & Prieto, L. P. (2022). Towards Data-Informed Teaching Practice: A Model for Integrating Analytics with Teacher Inquiry. Journal of Learning Analytics, 9(3), 88–103. https://doi.org/10.18608/jla.2022.7505
title: Design TLA models to start with purpose rather than problems, keep the inquiry question central, and complement student data with teaching data
description: The article derives design principles for analytics-informed teacher inquiry models from its three DBR iterations. A TLA model "should not focus on problems but should inform teaching practice in general", should "draw attention to an inquiry question", should indicate "how student data could be complemented by teaching data", and should help teachers "divide their teaching analysis into different but logically linked steps". These principles respond to teachers' difficulties with interpretation steps and their tendency to pose questions only about students.
requirements: Models should provide explanations, examples, and prompts for data variety to assist teachers at each step
constraints: The authors note more assistance should be provided to teachers in formulating inquiry questions, as teachers do not always start analysis with them
target_learners: Novice and experienced primary and secondary school teachers
target_learning_goals: Conducting analytics-informed inquiry into teaching practice
examples: The AMTI starts with "purpose" rather than "problem identification" and was reshaped into a circular diagram to emphasize iterative inquiry
key_sources: Saar, M., Rodríguez-Triana, M. J., & Prieto, L. P. (2022). Towards Data-Informed Teaching Practice: A Model for Integrating Analytics with Teacher Inquiry. Journal of Learning Analytics, 9(3), 88–103. https://doi.org/10.18608/jla.2022.7505

article_title: CRITICS - Critical Science Without Borders: Language Models to Promote Critical Thinking in Science Education
citation: Agerri, R., Aldabe, I., Cabrio, E., Cieliebak, M., Deriu, J., Flores, M., Kapočiūtė-Dzikienė, J., Kuizinienė, D., Rico, A., Ruiz-González, A., Soroa, A., Vaškevičius, M. and Villata, S. (2026). CRITICS - Critical Science Without Borders: Language Models to Promote Critical Thinking in Science Education. SEPLN 2026. https://www.hitz.eus/critics
title: Teaching and Learning Sequence (TLS) generator transforming translated scientific literature into structured educational resources
description: The second CRITICS component is a Teaching and Learning Sequence generator that investigates how to transform translated scientific literature into structured educational resources. It works "by analyzing the corpus to identify key concepts and pedagogical approaches, extracting argumentation graphs to generate TLSs". The TLSs specify driving problems/questions, learning objectives focused on competency acquisition, scientific practices including argumentation and critical thinking, and activities for science students, following Design-Based Research and curriculum-aligned teaching-learning.
requirements: argumentation graphs extracted from the corpus
alignment with learning objectives and competency acquisition
constraints: TLSs are developed for topic-specific competency-based assessments in natural sciences and AI
examples: The project cites prior work on teaching-learning sequences in initial teacher training about sound as the science education research tradition it follows.

article_title: Effects of Multimedia-Based Graphic Novel Presentation on Critical Thinking among Students of Different Learning Approaches
citation: Hii, S. C., & Fong, S. F. (2013). Effects of Multimedia-Based Graphic Novel Presentation on Critical Thinking among Students of Different Learning Approaches. TOJET: The Turkish Online Journal of Educational Technology, 12(4). https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ1080061
title: Mandell and Malone's Thinking Like a Historian (TLH) model as a framework for historical thinking in multimedia graphic novel learning
description: The Thinking Like a Historian (TLH) model by Mandell and Malone (2007) serves as a framework and historical literacy method in history teaching and learning. It identifies historical study as a three-step process: asking questions about the past, gathering sources and evaluating evidence, and drawing conclusions supported by evidence. The model organizes investigations through five categories of inquiry questions (Cause and Effect, Change and Continuity, Turning Points, Using the Past, Through Their Eyes) that engage students in historical meaning-making. In this study, the TLH model was incorporated into the design of a multimedia-based graphic novel learning environment to promote critical thinking skills in history learning rather than rote learning, embedding thought-provoking questions within the courseware.
requirements: Requires a constructivist learning environment with questioning approach to motivate learners to expand and find more about the subject area
constraints: The model was applied specifically to history learning about the Japanese Occupation of Malaya 1942-1945 with Malaysian secondary students
target_learning_goals: Critical thinking skills in history learning
Historical thinking skills including developing arguments from evidence
examples: The multimedia learning material 'Japanese Occupation of Malaya 1942-1945' embedded TLH inquiry questions to guide students through the three-step historical process
key_sources: Hii, S. C., & Fong, S. F. (2013). Effects of Multimedia-Based Graphic Novel Presentation on Critical Thinking among Students of Different Learning Approaches. TOJET: The Turkish Online Journal of Educational Technology, 12(4). https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ1018032
